column3: The Hebrew describes crying with a completed verb; BSB uses I cry.
The Hebrew explicitly names Your face; BSB says before You.
The Hebrew says my life has reached Sheol; BSB says draws near.
The Hebrew says free among the dead and cut off from Your hand; BSB says forsaken and from Your care.
The Hebrew separately names darknesses and depths; BSB combines them as darkest of the depths.
The Hebrew makes You the subject of afflicting with the waves; BSB makes all Your waves the subject submerging me.
The Hebrew names acquaintances rather than friends and describes not going out without an explicit cannot.
The Hebrew has eye in the singular and completed verbs of calling and spreading palms; BSB has eyes and present verbs.
The Hebrew has wonder in the singular and thanksgiving; BSB has wonders and praise.
The Hebrew has wonder in the singular; BSB has wonders.
The Hebrew describes crying as completed; BSB says I cry.
The Hebrew explicitly names my soul and does not repeat why before hiding the face as BSB does.
The Hebrew says dying rather than near death and presents affliction as a current state.
The Hebrew has burning angers in the plural; BSB has wrath.
The Hebrew uses completed verbs and says together; BSB uses present verbs and on every side.
The Hebrew says my acquaintances, darkness in a verbless phrase; BSB makes darkness my closest companion.
